title: Evidence-backed diagnosis of a failed SDDC Manager cluster expansion
prompt:
A cluster expansion failed on this VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 instance and the operator wants the failure diagnosed from the appliance's own records rather than guessed at. Implement the diagnosis in the stdlib-only vcfsupport package: fill in vcfsupport/client.py and vcfsupport/diagnose.py so that vcfsupport.diagnose_failure(base_url, username, password) returns the report dict described in README.md.

The run must authenticate with createToken, list the failed tasks, fetch the sub-task tree of the most recent one, read the appliance notifications, start a support bundle that collects exactly the logs the evidence implicates, poll it to a terminal status, retry the task, and report what it found. The root cause is the error on the deepest FAILED stage of the sub-task tree, and the components whose logs are worth collecting are the union of the resource types on every FAILED sub-task at any depth and on the notifications that correlate with the failure: severity ERROR or CRITICAL, not yet expired, and raised against the failed task's domain. README.md carries the report keys and the resource-type to Logs-flag mapping. Scope the support bundle to the failed task's DOMAIN resource and its CLUSTER resources, and never collect a log type the evidence does not implicate.

Use docs/contract.json as the REST contract and stay inside it: it names the seven operations SDDC Manager exposes here, their methods, paths, query parameters and request schemas, and its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Optional fields are optional on the wire - an optional request property or query parameter with no value must be absent from the request, not sent as null, an empty string, false, an empty array or an empty object. Use only the Python standard library; no third-party packages.

Run python3 tests/verify.py. Only vcfsupport/ is an implementation area; docs/ and tests/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
